clue.text: Clothes from Home Counties transported to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means reading right to left, so the pieces are turned round

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, where the counties around London lie
transported means borne, carried

explanation.surface: Garments brought over from the counties around London and shipped westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb. 'to the west' turns SEBORNE round. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to enrobe someone is to dress them in a robe or garment.

clue.text: Spots rebellious young rogue, finally put behind bars

indicators.note: rebellious letters will not stay in their order, so these four are rearranged

parts.note: spots on the skin are acne

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A pimply young delinquent is at last locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' rearranges ACNE to ENCA; 'finally' gives G and E, the last letters of 'young' and 'rogue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to encage is to shut in a cage, imprisoning as a jailer would.

clue.text: Weighty book penned by the Queen turned up far away

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
penned means enclosed, so the book goes inside the royal letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina
a tome is a large heavy book

explanation.surface: A heavy volume written by the monarch has surfaced somewhere distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts the book inside the royal cipher, and 'turned up' reverses the whole, as a down answer read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something remote lies at a great distance, out of reach.

clue.text: Sooty tries to pinch recipe for traditional nursery pie filling

parts.note: sooty means black

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip between, so the attempts close around the recipe letter

parts.note: tries means bids, attempts
R, the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A grimy cook has a go at stealing a recipe for the classic children's pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pinch' puts R inside BIDS to make BIRDS. Sing a Song of Sixpence has four and twenty of these baked in a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence tells of four and twenty such birds baked in a pie.

clue.text: Firm with no time for 50% of 3

definitions.note: the first half of the 3-down answer, a dark colour

indicators.note: with no means the time letter is taken away from the word for firm

parts.note: firm means stable, steady
T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A company with no time to spare for half of something.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of 3' points to the first half of the 3-down answer: the colour of those birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for that darkest colour, used in coats of arms.

clue.text: Lightweight Manx cat's a killer at sea

parts.note: a gram is a tiny unit of weight

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the last letter of the word for cat is docked

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A light little tailless cat turns out to be a deadly hunter of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' docks the tail of PUSS, since Manx cats, from the Isle of Man, are tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampus is an old name for the killer whale, also used for Risso's dolphin, a predator of the ocean.

clue.text: Queen by tradition always in the country, interminably

indicators.note: in places the word for always within the shortened country name
interminably means without an end, so the final letter of the country goes

parts.note: Guinea is a country in West Africa
always means ever

explanation.surface: A legendary monarch lives forever in the land, without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' drops the country's final A; 'in' then sets the word for always inside what is left, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend she is King Arthur's wife, so a queen of tradition rather than of history.

clue.text: Some decimals overlooked in addition

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few decimal places have been missed out as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run of letters inside 'decimals overlooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: as well, besides, too.

clue.text: Publish demand made by authority

indicators.note: made by puts the demand next to the authority, which comes first

parts.note: a pro is an expert, an authority
claim means demand

explanation.surface: An official body issues a demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'authority' here is an expert, a pro, not a governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to make known publicly, announce formally.

clue.text: Worker taking small females round shady bars

parts.note: S, the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: round says the letters for small and females surround the worker

parts.note: hens are female birds
a worker bee

explanation.surface: A labourer takes some little women around disreputable pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the worker inside the small-plus-females string; 'taking' is only a link. Shebeens are Irish in origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebeens are unlicensed drinking dens, originally Irish, hence of dubious reputation.

clue.text: One of 18 rounds about to come round

indicators.note: to come round means turning about, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: rounds of ammunition, ammo
C, circa, about

explanation.surface: Several rounds of something, about to come back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 18-across is the butterflies and moths, so 'One of 18' is a butterfly. 'to come round' reverses AMMOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a butterfly named for the small white comma-shaped mark on its underwing.

clue.text: One of 18 having weight on the borderline

indicators.note: on in an across answer puts the weight after the edge

parts.note: a brim is an edge or border
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Something heavy perched right on the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a pale yellow butterfly, one of the earliest seen in spring.

clue.text: One of 18 that might take its toll?

definitions.meaning: a keeper of a toll gate who collects payment from travellers

explanation.surface: A creature that might take its toll.
explanation.definitionFit: The gatekeeper is a hedge brown butterfly; literally it is someone guarding a gate, as on a toll road.

clue.text: Sportsman, could be one of 8 or 11 or one of 18

definitions.meaning: an Oxford or Cambridge athlete who has represented the university
a member of a rowing eight or a cricket or football eleven
a small butterfly, such as the common or holly kind

explanation.surface: An athlete who might be in a crew or team, or a winged creature.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' and '11' look like clue references but are team sizes: a rowing eight and an eleven. A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman who has competed against the rival university.
explanation.definitionFit: Blues are small butterflies; a Blue is also a university athlete honoured for competing in the varsity match.

clue.text: Forbidden pasty's finished outside

indicators.note: outside puts the word for finished around the word for pasty

parts.note: died means finished, came to an end
pasty as in pale-faced, sallow

explanation.surface: A pie is banned, eaten up outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the Cornish pie but is the adjective: pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something disallowed is not permitted, ruled out.

clue.text: Shut up about EC when one's admitted lack of accuracy

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the letter for one goes inside
about means surrounding, so the word for shut up goes round the two letters

parts.note: to shut up is to imprison
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Locking someone up over the European Community shows sloppiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: 'about' sets the clue's own EC inside the word for shut up, then 'admitted' lets in the numeral for one as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: imprecision is inexactness, the absence of precision.

clue.text: Press cutting? This could keep it in place

definitions.text: This could keep it in place

parts.note: the press is the newspapers, a paper
a clip is something cut or clipped

explanation.surface: Something to hold a newspaper cutting in position.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads back across the clue: 'it' is the press cutting just described.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire fastener holds loose sheets, such as a newspaper cutting, together.

clue.text: Liberal Catholic chucking one penny in hat

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so these letters are freely rearranged
chucking one and bringing a penny in swaps one letter for another

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral for one
P, the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A broad-minded churchgoer throws a coin into a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucking' with 'in' swaps the I in CATHOLIC for P to give CATHOLCP; 'Liberal' rearranges those letters. A cloth cap is the flat cap of the British working man.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a flat woollen cap, long associated with the British working class.

clue.text: Phantom PC alerts crook

indicators.note: crook as in crooked, bent out of shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A ghost policeman warns of a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal for the PC to catch, but it means bent, rearranging PC and ALERTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: ghostly, like an apparition.

clue.text: Polite padre converted large group of fliers

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A courteous chaplain won over a big flock of airmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' suggests pilots, but these are insects; 'converted' rearranges POLITE and PADRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific order of insects containing butterflies and moths, a large group with scaly wings.

clue.text: More delicate feature of Antarctic defaced

indicators.note: defaced means losing its face, the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a glacier, a river of ice found across the Antarctic

explanation.surface: Something finer about the polar landscape has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defaced' looks like vandalism but removes the first letter of GLACIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacier means more like lace, finer and more intricate in texture.

clue.text: Labour leader and I agree about church schools

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
about means around, so the agreeing word surrounds the church letters

parts.note: yes, said in agreement
CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: The party leader and I see eye to eye on faith schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church' tempts as part of the definition, 'church schools', but it supplies letters; 'about' puts them inside the word of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycées are French state secondary schools.

clue.text: Mark off second account

definitions.meaning: to check items off a list with a small mark
a moment, as in just a minute
credit, as in buying on account

explanation.surface: Cross off the second account.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'on tick' means on credit, and 'half a tick' means a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick means to check off, a moment (British informal), and credit, as in buying on tick.

clue.text: One of 18 Dominicans, say, could keep cash here, by the look of it

indicators.note: keep means hold within, so the friars' house holds the cash drawer

parts.note: Dominicans are an order of friars, who live in a friary
a till is where cash is kept

explanation.surface: Monks could store their money in this, by its appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the look of it' says the answer looks like a friary with a till in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritillaries are orange-brown butterflies with chequered markings.

clue.text: Experience worry over arresting good man

indicators.note: arresting means catching and holding, so the good man goes inside
over in a down answer means turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry them
ST, saint, a good man

explanation.surface: Undergo anxiety about detaining a virtuous fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worry' here is the sense in 'what's eating you?'; 'over' turns that word upside down, and 'arresting' holds the saint inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to taste freedom is to experience it.

clue.text: Fellow dropped by United brought into play

indicators.note: dropped means left out, so the fellow letter is removed

parts.note: fused means joined, united
F, the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A player is dropped by Manchester United and brought on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' suggests a football team, but it is fused.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something used has been employed, put to work.

clue.text: Potentially one of 18 lyrics has to be revamped

indicators.note: revamped means remade, so these letters are refashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: Song words need to be rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' rearranges LYRICS and HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa is the stage before the adult butterfly, so it is a potential one.

clue.text: Leading chess player's member of 18

definitions.meaning: the side in chess that moves first
a butterfly such as the cabbage kind

explanation.surface: The top chess player belongs to some group.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pale pieces always open the game; cabbage and marbled varieties are butterflies.

clue.text: Youngster, running round shop from rear, caused a crash

indicators.note: running round means surrounding, so the young one goes about the shop

parts.note: a pup is a young animal

indicators.note: from rear means read from the back, so the shop is backwards

parts.note: a deli, a delicatessen

explanation.surface: A kid sprinting around a shop knocked things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from rear' reads the shop word backwards and 'running round' wraps the young animal around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile up is to crash, especially of vehicles colliding one after another.

clue.text: On the base, nursed sick bears

indicators.note: on in an across answer puts the rearranged letters after the base letter

parts.note: e, the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: sick means unwell, out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: At the military base, the sick were nursed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp, but e is the base of natural logarithms; 'sick' rearranges NURSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to bear something is to put up with it, tolerate it.
